name: MathlibAnnex.convexHull_maxSlice_eq_supportFace
title: A support face is the convex hull of the maximizing generators

content.display_title: A support face is the convex hull of the maximizing generators
content.one_sentence_role: Identifies the points of a convex hull on a supporting level by discarding generators with zero weight.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space and let $\ell$ be a continuous linear functional. Set

$$m=\max_{x\in K}\ell(x),\qquad K_\ell=\{x\in K:\ell(x)=m\}.$$

Then

$$\operatorname{conv}(K_\ell)=\{z\in\operatorname{conv}(K):\ell(z)=m\}.$$

The right side is the support face at the maximum of $\ell$.
content.assumptions: The ambient space is a finite-dimensional real normed vector space. The set $K$ is nonempty and compact, and $\ell$ is continuous and real-linear. The set $K$ need not be convex; $\ell$ may be zero.
content.conclusion: The entire support face is generated by the original points of $K$ at which $\ell$ attains its maximum. In particular, one need not introduce new generators from the interior of the convex hull.
content.proof_summary: One inclusion follows from convexity of a level set. For the reverse inclusion, a convex representation at the maximum has zero total gap, forcing every positive-weight generator to lie at that maximum.

proof_steps.text:
The maximum exists because $K$ is nonempty compact and $\ell$ is continuous. Put $H=\{x:\ell(x)=m\}$. Linearity makes $H$ convex, and $K_\ell\subseteq K\cap H$. Hence

$$\operatorname{conv}(K_\ell)
\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(K)\cap H.$$

Here the first containment uses both monotonicity of the convex hull and convexity of $H$. It remains valid when $\ell=0$.

Conversely, let $z\in\operatorname{conv}(K)$ satisfy $\ell(z)=m$. Choose a finite convex representation $z=\sum_i t_ix_i$ with $x_i\in K$, $t_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i t_i=1$. Each gap $m-\ell(x_i)$ is nonnegative, and linearity gives

$$\sum_i t_i(m-\ell(x_i))=m\sum_i t_i-\ell\left(\sum_i t_ix_i\right)=m-\ell(z)=0.$$

A finite sum of nonnegative terms is zero only if every term is zero. Therefore $t_i>0$ implies $m-\ell(x_i)=0$, so $x_i\in K_\ell$.

Remove the zero-weight terms. The remaining weights still sum to $1$, their weighted sum is still $z$, and every remaining generator belongs to $K_\ell$. Thus $z\in\operatorname{conv}(K_\ell)$, proving the reverse inclusion and the equality.

content.lean_realization_notes: Continuity and compactness give a maximizer in $K$, so $K_\ell$ is nonempty. It is the intersection of $K$ with the closed level set $\ell^{-1}(\{m\})$, hence compact. These two facts make the maximum slice eligible for another refinement; membership in that refined set is precisely membership in $K$ together with equality to the maximum.
